newsitem.title: BELARUS: Political opponents sign compromise deal
newsitem.headline: Political opponents sign compromise deal

text.p: Political opponents in Belarus signed a compromise deal on Friday to resolve a standoff which threatened stability in the former Soviet republic.

Journalists watched as President Alexander Lukashenko, Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Belarus parliament speaker Semyon Sharetksy and the speakers of Russia's two houses of parliament signed the agreement.
Lukashenko said he had agreed that the results of a referendum on extending his powers would not be binding and that the parliament would not try to impeach him.

"In this agreement the president removes two decrees concerning the binding nature of the referendum vote. Parliament withdraws from the constitutional court all the materials connected to the impeachement," Lukashenko said.

The deal, called "An agreement about the social poltiical situation and consitutional reforms of the republic of Belarus," was designed to end a standoff between opposing political forces which threatened stability in the republic.
